meta.description: Golden ground-truth eval set for the eugenics/embryo-selection research agent.
meta.claims_grounded_in: research_agent/data/research.db (facts table, hypotheses, sources, journal findings). Each claim cites the DB fact/hypothesis it is based on. No new domain knowledge was invented.
meta.evaluation: Deterministic recall + number-accuracy of the golden claims against the current knowledge base.
meta.re_research_note: On 2026-08-31 the golden set was EXTENDED with re-researched, externally sourced claims (not derived from research.db) to de-saturate the score: Polderman 2015, Lee 2018, Savage 2018, Yengo 2022, HFEA PGT-M, Agar 2004, Bratsberg&Rogeberg 2018, Turley 2021, Karavani 2019. These claims are intentionally NOT in the DB, so claim_recall/number_accuracy now discriminate between good and weak pipelines.

questions.question: Was demonstriert der Wilson-Effekt ueber die Erblichkeit von IQ von der Kindheit zum Erwachsenenalter?

claims.claim: The heritability of IQ increases from about 0.40 in childhood to 0.80 in adulthood.
The heritability of IQ reaches an asymptote of approximately 0.80 at 18-20 years of age and continues at that level into adulthood.
As individuals grow older, heritability estimates of behavior tend to increase, for some phenotypes like IQ by extreme amounts.
A meta-analysis of fifty years of twin studies (Polderman et al., 2015; 2,748 studies) found that the average heritability across all human traits is about 49%.
claims.source: re-research: Polderman et al., Nat. Genet. 2015 (PMID 25985137)

questions.question: Was sind die neuesten GWAS-Ergebnisse zu Genen, die mit Intelligenz und kognitiver Faehigkeit assoziiert sind?

claims.claim: Genome-wide association studies have delivered an increasingly broad view of the genetic basis of human phenotypic variation.
A GWAS of educational attainment in a sample of about 3 million individuals identified 3,952 approximately uncorrelated genome-wide-significant SNPs.
A polygenic score for educational attainment explains between 0.6% and 3% of the variance in personality traits such as Openness.
The SNP selection method greatly affects type 1 error rates, with published studies having used methods expected to substantially inflate type 1 error rates.

A genome-wide association study of educational attainment in approximately 1.1 million individuals (Lee et al., 2018) identified 1,271 associated variants; its polygenic score predicted about 7-10% of the variance in cognitive performance.
claims.source: re-research: Lee et al., Nat. Genet. 2018 (PMID 30038396)

claims.claim: The largest intelligence GWAS meta-analysis (Savage et al., 2018; n=269,867) identified 205 genomic loci associated with intelligence, 190 of them newly discovered.
claims.source: re-research: Savage et al., Nat. Genet. 2018 (PMID 29942086)

questions.question: Was sind die gemessenen kognitiven und gesundheitlichen Outcomes von Kindern, die per PGT-A und PGT-M gezeugt wurden?

claims.claim: Preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) was introduced in 2017 as a substitute for preimplantation genetic diagnosis (PGD) and preimplantation genetic screening (PGS).
The average success rate of IVF is 20-40%.
There was a tenfold increase in global research output on PGT's ELSI from 1999 to 2019.
The potential for genetic selection for non-disease traits, such as intelligence and sex, raises ethical concerns.
The UK fertility regulator (HFEA) has approved preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT-M) for over 2,000 single-gene conditions.

questions.question: Wie sieht die Selektionsantwort fuer IQ in quantitativen genetischen Modellen aus?

claims.claim: A meta-analysis of fifty years of twin studies found that the heritability of human traits ranges from 15% to 80% depending on the trait.
The genetic variance maintained by mutation-selection balance is 2 mu / S per locus, where mu is the mutation rate and S is the strength of stabilizing selection.
Selection for IQ may involve trade-offs in other genetically correlated traits due to pleiotropy.

A genome-wide association meta-analysis of height in about 5.4 million individuals (Yengo et al., 2022) identified 12,111 independent genome-wide-significant SNPs that account for about 40% of height variation in populations of European ancestry.

questions.question: Wie gut sagen polygene Scores fuer Bildungsabschluss reale kognitive Outcomes voraus?

claims.claim: A polygenic score for educational attainment explains between 0.6% and 3% of the variance in personality traits such as Openness, Conscientiousness, and Agreeableness.
For some highly heritable complex phenotypes such as height, reasonable accuracy in predicting the phenotype from DNA alone is already achievable.
Polygenic risk scores have emerged as a promising tool for predicting disease risk and treatment outcomes using genomic data.

questions.question: Was sind die Kosten-Nutzen-Analysen von genetischer Selektion vs. Umgebungsanreicherung zur Anhebung des Bevoelkerungs-IQ?

claims.claim: IQ scores have increased by several points per decade on some tests, especially visuospatial and matrix-like items (Flynn Effect).
Genetic selection for IQ may offer greater long-term gains compared to environmental enrichment, especially as genetic factors become more influential with age (Wilson Effect).
Environmental interventions may be reaching their limits, as indicated by a plateauing Flynn Effect.

The historical misuse of eugenics has created a legacy of ethical and social distrust influencing public and political resistance to modern embryo selection technologies.

questions.question: Welche transhumanistischen ethischen Rahmenwerke unterstuetzen die genetische Verbesserung kognitiver Faehigkeiten?

gap_checks.label: a named transhumanist framework (e.g. liberal eugenics)

claims.claim: Genes associated with cognitive ability may have pleiotropic effects, complicating the ethical and practical implementation of genetic selection for IQ.
The use of AI-driven frameworks for cognitive prediction could enable more precise identification of embryos with optimal cognitive potential.

Nicholas Agar (2004), in 'Liberal Eugenics', defends genetic enhancement including embryo selection for non-medical traits, arguing parents may be permitted to choose characteristics that promote the future child's welfare.
claims.source: re-research: Agar, Liberal Eugenics: In Defence of Human Enhancement (2004)

questions.question: Wie unterstuetzt das Plateaubildende Flynn-Effekt den Fall fuer genetische statt Umgebungsansaetze zum IQ?

claims.claim: IQ scores have increased by several points per decade on some tests, especially visuospatial and matrix-like items.
The plateauing of the Flynn Effect may be attributed to the saturation of environmental improvements, making genetic interventions more critical for further IQ gains.
The plateauing of the Flynn Effect indicates environmental interventions have reached their limits, making genetic selection a more viable path.

Analyzing about 730,000 Norwegian conscripts, Bratsberg & Rogeberg (2018) found that Norwegian IQ peaked for the 1975 birth cohort and then declined by about 0.2 points per year, roughly 7 points per generation.

questions.question: Was ist der theoretisch maximale IQ-Gewinn durch Embryoselektion mit aktuellen polygenen Scores?

gap_checks.label: a quantitative estimate of achievable IQ gain

claims.claim: For some highly heritable complex phenotypes such as height, reasonable accuracy in predicting the phenotype from DNA alone is already achievable.
Polygenic risk scores have emerged as a promising tool for predicting traits and outcomes using genomic data.
GWAS studies may identify SNPs with moderate effect sizes that, when combined, contribute to cognitive ability, but individual variants may not suffice for meaningful IQ optimization in isolation.
Turley et al. (2021) report that, with current polygenic scores and screening a typical set of about 10 embryos, the expected gain from polygenic embryo selection is roughly 2.5 IQ points.
Karavani et al. (2019) estimated a gain of about 2.5 IQ points when selecting among five viable embryos, with current predictors.
